Health service spatial accessibility matrices for Aotearoa New Zealand: Estimated travel time from geospatial unit to every Hospital, Pharmacy, General Practitioner service, and Cancer Treatment facility
recent_works.abstract: Aim: A national suite of spatial accessibility matrices designed for non-specialist users in Aotearoa New Zealand was developed with the goal of providing flexible, high resolution, travel time and distance datasets that enable equitable, spatially informed health service planning.Method: Using New Zealand address weighted centroids for Meshblock, SA1, SA2, and Domicile code geographies, shortest path drive times and distances were estimated to GP, pharmacy, hospital, and cancer treatment facilities; and for each SA2 code pairing. Seventeen national travel-time and distance matrices were produced. Validation against 17,000 Google Maps Distance Matrix API samples assessed correlation between estimated and reference travel times and distances.Data: An industry standard road network was used for this analysis. The Precisely (2025) Street Pro Navigation Premium NZ Road Network topologically models the roads, junctions, and traffic directions of the physical road system. Each road segment is associated with a distance and speed impedance. Data on road speeds is derived through aggregate measurement of active vehicles by TomTom.
